title: Metric Gateway: smart sampling, label enrichment, and lightweight aggregation for inference KPIs
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight Metric Gateway (MGW) sitting between inference hosts and our OTLP/Prometheus ingestion layer to provide three capabilities: 1) smart, deterministic sampling for high-cardinality inference telemetry; 2) label enrichment and normalization close to the source to reduce downstream fanout; 3) configurable micro-aggregation for short retention KPIs to reduce cost while preserving SLO observability.

Background: Our current pipeline sends high-cardinality labels (model_version, model_size, route, prompt_category, customer_tier) for every request to the central ingestion fabric. At scale this produces heavy cardinality spikes and increased ingestion costs, and downstream Prometheus job scraping becomes brittle during bursts. We need an edge component that enforces consistent label vocabularies, applies adaptive sampling based on request characteristics, and emits both raw and aggregated KPI streams so SLA dashboards remain accurate.

Design summary:
- Deploy MGW as a sidecar on inference nodes (host-level) with a central control plane for sampling policies.
- Input: OTLP metrics + light JSON labels. MGW will: 1) normalize labels (canonicalize model names, drop transient route ids), 2) enrich with inferred fields (approx_token_count, inferred_latency_bucket, model_variant_family), 3) deterministically sample 1-in-N requests for full-detail export and emit micro-aggregates (p50/p90/p99 counts and error rates) every 10s to the metrics fabric.
- Sampling policy is workload-aware: baseline sampling for small models is lower (more detail retained), large model/generative workloads use higher sampling; additional weight added for requests that spike latency or errors to preserve anomaly visibility.
- Two parallel outputs: a high-cardinality OTLP stream (sampled) routed to the long-term ingestion cluster, and a Prometheus-friendly aggregated stream (low-cardinality) routed to our metrics cache. Both streams include a deterministic sample_id so traces and sampled metrics can be correlated offline.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end test showing 70% reduction in unique label cardinality seen by ingest during a synthetic burst while preserving >=95% of SLA breach events in sampled stream.
- Prometheus scrape latency remains within SLO during 10x traffic bursts in staging.
- Dashboards updated to use aggregated stream for KPI heatmaps and sampled stream for root cause investigations.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Enrichment logic in-sidecar increases CPU on inference hosts; benchmark target: <2% p99 CPU overhead for canonical workloads.
- Deterministic sampling can drop low-frequency but important signals; mitigation: anomaly override rules and emergency full-sample mode.
- Additional operational complexity in policy rollout; will build UI controls and versioned policy bundles.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): sidecars on 5% of hosts in us-west with read-only policy, collect metrics but do not alter exports.
- Phase 2 (gradual): enable sampling/enrichment for 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring gates at each step.
- Phase 3: enable micro-aggregation export path and switch dashboards to aggregated streams with parallel verification against raw data for two weeks.

Instrumentation mapping:
- Map current metric names to normalized names (e.g., inference.latency_ms -> rw.inference.latency_ms.normalized).
- Emit aggregated labels: model_family, model_size_bucket, route_group, tier.
- Preserve trace_id/span_id linkage by embedding sample_id in metric labels and OTLP resource attributes.

Operational notes:
- Control plane exposes a REST endpoint for policy updates and a Prometheus endpoint for MGW health.
- Log format: structured JSON with sampling decisions and enrichment annotations for debugging; logs shipped to centralized logstore with retention policy.

Documentation and QA:
- Confluence design doc: confluence/redwood/metrics-gateway-design (link below).
- Load-test harness and synthetic burst scenarios added to infra repo.

Estimated effort: 5 points (sidecar implementation + control plane + dashboard migration).
comments: 2025-07-16: Spike complete. Proof-of-concept sidecar implemented in Go using OpenTelemetry SDK. Deterministic sampling uses stable hashing on (request_id, model_version, epoch). CPU overhead measured at ~1.1% in medium load test.
2025-07-20: Design review with Observability and Runtime teams. Decision: micro-aggregation window set to 10s to balance resolution and cardinality. Need to define canonical label vocab with Product.

2025-07-24: PR opened - infra#5421. Initial integration tests failing when label normalization drops 'route' (some dashboards relied on route id). Action: add route_group fallback and update dashboards in parallel.

2025-07-28: Canaries deployed to 5% hosts in us-west. Observed 62% reduction in unique label combinations to ingestion fabric during a synthetic prompt-flood. Two late-night alerts triggered; root cause was a missing fallback for empty model_variant -> fixed in hotpatch.
2025-08-01: UX/PM requested ability to temporarily disable sampling per-customer for debugging; added policy flag and RBAC check. Planning canary expansion to 25% next week.
2025-08-02: Security reviewed enrichment fields — no PII added. KMS access not required for MGW. Marked security_review_required = false.
